reviewer: Pickle: footwear heat damage and leather shrinkage, shoe microclimate, foot odour microbiology, dermatophyte survival in footwear, de-icing salt leather damage, UV steriliser safety, desiccant capacity, PFAS repellent regulation, and Coupang/Kakao product terms
method: Reviewed the draft against the 26 recorded facts and 30 listed citations on 2026-11-13. Hair dryer heat: the NBSIR 76-1112 report measured outlet air temperature 2.5 cm from the opening at 45, 54, 58, 66, 67, 75 and 86 degrees Celsius across 15 commercial dryers, and a 1,200 W Rowenta unit was reported at 108 C, so the article gives a 45 to 108 C range rather than a single number. Leather: NBS Circular 458 gives a shrinkage temperature of about 60 to 65 C for fresh untanned collagen, while SATRA notes chrome-tanned leather can reach about 120 C and alum or vegetable tannages stay at or below 85 C; Solangi et al. (2023) measured 18 to 41 percent dry-heat area shrinkage in three shoe-upper leathers, so the article says heat changes leather rather than claiming every boot shrinks at 60 C. Nike's official shoe-care page states heat damages the glue holding soles and can shrink shoes, advises never exposing shoes to blow-dryer heat for more than a few minutes, and gives about 12 hours for natural drying. KCA 2018: of 121 summer-footwear cases reviewed, 81 were product defects, durability failure was 40.7 percent (33 cases) with thermal shrinkage and leather damage among its causes, and design and adhesion defects were 16.1 percent (13 cases) each. In-shoe climate: West et al. (Applied Ergonomics 2019) report 35.2 to 36.1 C and 75.8 to 84.1 percent relative humidity at the end of a 50-minute run rising to 87.5 percent in recovery; Irzmanska (AUTEX 2015) reports 35.8 to 37.3 C, 79 to 80 percent in leather footwear and 96.6 percent in vapour-resistant rubber boots. Foot sweat: Taylor et al. (2006) measured about 30 mL per hour per foot with a 50 mL peak in the final five minutes; the 250,000 sweat glands per foot figure is from Maastricht UMC patient information. Odour: Ara et al. (Can J Microbiol 2006) identify isovaleric acid from leucine degradation by Staphylococcus epidermidis; Stevens et al. (FEMS Microbiol Ecol 2014) show plantar dominance of staphylococci and isovaleric acid absent on the dorsal foot. Mould and dermatophytes: Tsongas and Riordan (ASHRAE Journal 2016) give 80 percent as the germination threshold and 85 percent for visible growth and note leather goods in closets grow mould well below 80 percent. Lee et al. (Korean J Med Mycol 2001) isolated dermatophytes from 33 of 70 adult slippers (47.1 percent); Knudsen (1987) from 41 percent of footwear of tinea pedis patients; Ishijima et al. (2019) from safety shoes of 6 of 9 patients. Essien et al. (2009) give D80 values of 3.2 minutes for T. rubrum, 4.0 for T. mentagrophytes and 4.4 for E. floccosum, and Hammer et al. report T. rubrum surviving 30 C washing but eliminated at 60 C, which is why the article says a 45 to 55 C dryer dries rather than sterilises. Prevalence: the MOHW/NHIS 2015 release reports 830,802 foot-ringworm patients in 2013; Yoon et al. (Epidemiol Health 2014) report 5.2 percent dermatophytosis prevalence. Calcium chloride: the KCA analysis of 134 Ugg-boot complaints from 2008 to November 2010 found 53 washing and hardening cases, 52 quality defects and 25 e-commerce cases, and states road de-icing calcium chloride hardens leather; Cleanopia's customer FAQ likewise attributes hardened natural leather to de-icing calcium chloride, and calcium chloride's deliquescent behaviour is documented in desiccant technical material. The article therefore describes brine drawing water out osmotically and the leather losing its oil balance rather than asserting a measured oil-loss figure. UV: the KCA 2020 survey of 25 DC-powered UV sterilisers found 3 emitting only UV-A, 21 without eye and skin shielding, and one with ozone at five times the 0.1 ppm limit; UV-C acts only on surfaces it reaches. PTC drying: Rosly et al. (ECOSIA 2026) dried sports shoes in 24 minutes at 45 C with 0.874 to 1.674 kWh per cycle and note the self-limiting PTC characteristic; Samsung's Shoe Dresser material gives sub-40 C drying and 8.8 times faster than natural drying. Desiccants: Delta Adsorbents lists 33 percent minimum water uptake at 80 percent RH and 22 percent at 40 percent RH for type A silica gel; CCI Technical Bulletin 33 gives 27.07 percent equilibrium moisture content at 50 percent RH and 120 C regeneration. Repellents: Hill et al. (Chemosphere 2017) show non-fluorinated finishes match fluorinated water repellency while lacking oil repellency; Lee et al. (Environ Pollut 2026) assess PFAS emissions from water-repellent sprays; Denmark's 2024/0646/DK notification bans PFAS above limits in consumer clothing, footwear and waterproofing agents from July 2026. Humidity: Cho and Choi (KIEAE 2013) measured a 35.4 percent winter mean across 20 apartments with 6 units at 26.7 percent, against the KDCA's 45 to 55 percent recommendation. Products: the three Coupang listings were opened in the browser on 2026-11-13. Cleanfree FU-C2400BE portable UV sterilising dryer at 25,900 won after 42 percent off 45,000 won with 567 reviews at 4.5, free shipping and returns, USB-C power and timer, with 50 C drying temperature and 190 g weight read from reviews; Anjeopso waterproof spray 200 mL at 12,000 won after 24 percent off 15,900 won with 8,538 reviews at 4.5 and more than 4,000 buyers in a month; Ilima deodorising and dehumidifying packs 75 g by 4 at 8,530 won with 595 reviews at 5.0, fragrance-free bamboo charcoal and monthly sun-drying. The Sourcing Zero DSHJ-S-1904 listing was rejected for the top slot because reviews state it has no timer and needs about nine hours. The Kakao Gift curator link gift-link.kakao.com/c/3c1bTbXz was created on 2026-11-13 for the Purecoach four-arm shoe dryer at 50,000 won discounted to 40,500 won, 12 gift reviews at 4.0, 700 wishes and expected commission of 4,500 won, with the required curator disclosure in the article. Affiliate deep links were built from the pageKey, itemId and vendorItemId read on each product page. Gate score 100/100 with 125 of 125 numbers backed by the research file.
